Fitting IRT models

fitting-irt-models.Rmd

Note: The content of this vignette was generated using Claude agents and then reviewed by package authors.

LEVANTE task scores are ability estimates from item response theory (IRT) models fit with mirt. This vignette shows how to fit those models for one task with levantemodels: what the input data looks like, the calls that fit the models, and how to work with the model files they write. (For scoring data against models that have already been fit, see vignette("scoring-and-model-registry").)

The vignette uses simulated data so that it runs offline in a few seconds. The last section shows how to build the same input from real LEVANTE data.

library(levantemodels)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

Input data

The fitting functions take trial-level data nested by task and by group: one row per combination of task and grouping variables, with the trials in a list-column called data.

Here we simulate a 4-alternative task (chance = 0.25) given at two sites. Children at site_a (English) saw 15 items, and children at site_b (German) saw only the first 12 of them. Responses follow a 2PL model with a guessing floor at chance.

set.seed(1)

items <- tibble(
  item_uid = sprintf("matrix_%02d", 1:15),
  a = rlnorm(15, 0, 0.3),              # discrimination
  b = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 15),     # difficulty
  chance = 0.25
)

simulate_site <- \(dataset, language, n_runs, theta_mean, item_uids) {
  tibble(dataset, language,
         run_id = paste0(dataset, "_run", 1:n_runs),
         theta = rnorm(n_runs, theta_mean)) |>
    cross_join(filter(items, item_uid %in% item_uids)) |>
    mutate(p = chance + (1 - chance) * plogis(a * (theta - b)),
           correct = runif(n()) < p) |>
    select(dataset, language, run_id, item_uid, chance, correct)
}

trials <- bind_rows(
  simulate_site("site_a", "en-US", 400, 0.0, items$item_uid),
  simulate_site("site_b", "de-DE", 300, 0.5, items$item_uid[1:12])
)

task_data <- trials |>
  mutate(item_task = "matrix") |>
  nest(data = -c(item_task, dataset, language))

task_data
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   dataset language item_task data                
#>   <chr>   <chr>    <chr>     <list>              
#> 1 site_a  en-US    matrix    <tibble [6,000 × 4]>
#> 2 site_b  de-DE    matrix    <tibble [3,600 × 4]>

Each element of data holds one row per trial:

task_data$data[[1]]
#> # A tibble: 6,000 × 4
#>    run_id      item_uid  chance correct
#>    <chr>       <chr>      <dbl> <lgl>  
#>  1 site_a_run1 matrix_01   0.25 TRUE   
#>  2 site_a_run1 matrix_02   0.25 FALSE  
#>  3 site_a_run1 matrix_03   0.25 FALSE  
#>  4 site_a_run1 matrix_04   0.25 TRUE   
#>  5 site_a_run1 matrix_05   0.25 TRUE   
#>  6 site_a_run1 matrix_06   0.25 TRUE   
#>  7 site_a_run1 matrix_07   0.25 TRUE   
#>  8 site_a_run1 matrix_08   0.25 FALSE  
#>  9 site_a_run1 matrix_09   0.25 FALSE  
#> 10 site_a_run1 matrix_10   0.25 TRUE   
#> # ℹ 5,990 more rows

The columns the fitting functions need are:

Column Level Contents
item_task outer task name, used to select a task and to name output files
grouping variable(s) outer e.g. language, dataset, site: what models are fit separately for, or what groups multigroup models compare
run_id data one task administration; each run becomes one row of the response matrix
item_uid data item identifier; an item that is answered more than once in a run is treated as several instances whose parameters are constrained to be equal
correct data response (logical or 0/1); NA responses are dropped
chance data chance level for the item, used as its fixed lower asymptote (guessing parameter)

Before fitting, items with no variance in responses are dropped. For multigroup models, items without variance within some group are also dropped.

Specifying the models

Models are specified as a data frame with one row per model. For pooled models (fit separately for each subset of the data) the columns are nfact (number of factors) and itemtype ("Rasch" or "2PL"). For multigroup models there’s also invariance, which says what is constrained to be equal across groups:

  • "configural": nothing is shared, so each group has its own item parameters.
  • "metric": slopes are shared.
  • "scalar": slopes and intercepts are shared, and group means and variances are freely estimated.

(See invariances for the mapping to mirt arguments.)

models_pooled <- tribble(
  ~nfact, ~itemtype,
       1,   "Rasch",
       1,     "2PL"
)

models_multigroup <- tribble(
  ~nfact, ~itemtype, ~invariance,
       1,   "Rasch", "configural",
       1,   "Rasch", "scalar",
       1,     "2PL", "configural",
       1,     "2PL", "metric",
       1,     "2PL", "scalar"
)

Priors are a named list: each name is a mirt parameter, and each value gives the prior type and its two parameters. These are the priors that LEVANTE uses:

priors <- list(d = c("norm", 0, 3), a1 = c("norm", 1, 0.3))

Fitting

The fitting functions write each fitted model to registry_dir as a ModelRecord saved in an .rds file, and they are called for this side effect. Models are fit with verbose mirt output, which we hide here.

registry_dir <- "model_registry"

Pooled models by language. fit_bylanguage_task() fits every model in models_pooled separately for each language in the data. fit_task_models_pooled() does the same for a single subset of any variable, e.g. subset_var = dataset, subset_val = "site_a".

fit_bylanguage_task(task_data, models = models_pooled, priors = priors,
                    task = "matrix", registry_dir = registry_dir)

Multigroup models. fit_task_models_multigroup() fits one model with every level of group as a group, for each row of models_multigroup:

fit_task_models_multigroup(task_data, models = models_multigroup,
                           priors = priors, task = "matrix", group = dataset,
                           registry_dir = registry_dir)

Each multigroup specification is fit in up to two steps:

  1. overlap_items/: a model fit to just the items that every group saw (here, the 12 items common to both sites).
  2. all_items/: a model fit to all items. Parameters for the overlapping items are fixed at their values from step 1, so these items anchor the scale and the remaining items are calibrated onto it. This step is skipped for configural models, since they put no constraints across groups.

The resulting registry:

list.files(registry_dir, recursive = TRUE)
#>  [1] "matrix/by_language/de-DE/matrix_2pl_f1.rds"                            
#>  [2] "matrix/by_language/de-DE/matrix_rasch_f1.rds"                          
#>  [3] "matrix/by_language/en-US/matrix_2pl_f1.rds"                            
#>  [4] "matrix/by_language/en-US/matrix_rasch_f1.rds"                          
#>  [5] "matrix/multigroup_dataset/all_items/matrix_2pl_f1_metric.rds"          
#>  [6] "matrix/multigroup_dataset/all_items/matrix_2pl_f1_scalar.rds"          
#>  [7] "matrix/multigroup_dataset/all_items/matrix_rasch_f1_scalar.rds"        
#>  [8] "matrix/multigroup_dataset/overlap_items/matrix_2pl_f1_configural.rds"  
#>  [9] "matrix/multigroup_dataset/overlap_items/matrix_2pl_f1_metric.rds"      
#> [10] "matrix/multigroup_dataset/overlap_items/matrix_2pl_f1_scalar.rds"      
#> [11] "matrix/multigroup_dataset/overlap_items/matrix_rasch_f1_configural.rds"
#> [12] "matrix/multigroup_dataset/overlap_items/matrix_rasch_f1_scalar.rds"

Paths follow the pattern {task}/{model_set}/{subset}/{task}_{itemtype}_f{nfact}[_{invariance}].rds. This is the same layout as the LEVANTE model registry on Redivis: each row of the scoring table (fetch_scoring_table()) gives a model_set, subset, itemtype, nfact, and invariance, and model_spec_filename() turns these into a path in this layout.

Working with model files

Each file contains a ModelRecord, a lightweight record of the fitted model that holds its parameters, the data it was fit to, its fit statistics, and the EAP ability scores for the data it was fit to.

mod_rec <- readRDS(file.path(registry_dir,
                             "matrix/multigroup_dataset/all_items/matrix_2pl_f1_scalar.rds"))
mod_rec
#> ModelRecord of a MultipleGroupClass model (1 factor 2PL)

Item parameters. mod_coefs() returns one row per item and group, with slope (a1), intercept (d), lower and upper asymptotes (g, u), difficulty on the IRT scale (-d / a1), and the number of responses to the item. Under scalar invariance the parameters are the same for both groups. Items 13–15 have no responses from site_b, but they still get that group’s (shared) parameters.

mod_coefs(mod_rec)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 9
#>    group  item         a1     d     g     u n_responses n_inst difficulty
#>    <chr>  <chr>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>       <int>  <int>      <dbl>
#>  1 site_a matrix_02 1.01  1.84   0.25     1         400      1      -1.82
#>  2 site_b matrix_02 1.01  1.84   0.25     1         300      1      -1.82
#>  3 site_a matrix_01 1.05  1.72   0.25     1         400      1      -1.64
#>  4 site_b matrix_01 1.05  1.72   0.25     1         300      1      -1.64
#>  5 site_a matrix_04 1.28  1.85   0.25     1         400      1      -1.44
#>  6 site_b matrix_04 1.28  1.85   0.25     1         300      1      -1.44
#>  7 site_a matrix_03 0.783 1.08   0.25     1         400      1      -1.38
#>  8 site_b matrix_03 0.783 1.08   0.25     1         300      1      -1.38
#>  9 site_a matrix_05 0.835 0.883  0.25     1         400      1      -1.06
#> 10 site_b matrix_05 0.835 0.883  0.25     1         300      1      -1.06
#> # ℹ 20 more rows

Ability scores. scores() returns EAP ability estimates and their standard errors for each run the model was fit to:

scores(mod_rec)
#> # A tibble: 700 × 3
#>    run_id       ability    se
#>    <chr>          <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1 site_a_run1   -0.600 0.643
#>  2 site_a_run2    0.230 0.673
#>  3 site_a_run3    0.924 0.636
#>  4 site_a_run4   -0.738 0.607
#>  5 site_a_run5    1.07  0.665
#>  6 site_a_run6    0.892 0.641
#>  7 site_a_run7   -0.161 0.675
#>  8 site_a_run8   -0.119 0.648
#>  9 site_a_run9   -1.10  0.646
#> 10 site_a_run10  -0.585 0.674
#> # ℹ 690 more rows

As a check, the estimates approximately recover the simulated difference between sites (site_b was simulated 0.5 SD higher):

scores(mod_rec) |>
  mutate(group = mod_rec@groups) |>
  summarise(mean_ability = mean(ability), .by = group)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   group  mean_ability
#>   <chr>         <dbl>
#> 1 site_a     0.000445
#> 2 site_b     0.558

Model comparison. AIC(), BIC(), and logLik() work on a ModelRecord. Models are only comparable when they’re fit to the same data, so here we compare the five overlap_items models:

overlap_dir <- file.path(registry_dir, "matrix/multigroup_dataset/overlap_items")
overlap_files <- list.files(overlap_dir, full.names = TRUE)

tibble(model = basename(overlap_files),
       mod_rec = lapply(overlap_files, readRDS)) |>
  mutate(logLik = sapply(mod_rec, logLik),
         AIC = sapply(mod_rec, AIC),
         BIC = sapply(mod_rec, BIC)) |>
  select(-mod_rec) |>
  arrange(BIC)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   model                          logLik   AIC   BIC
#>   <chr>                           <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 matrix_rasch_f1_scalar.rds     -4491. 9011. 9079.
#> 2 matrix_2pl_f1_scalar.rds       -4483. 9017. 9135.
#> 3 matrix_rasch_f1_configural.rds -4483. 9019. 9137.
#> 4 matrix_2pl_f1_metric.rds       -4477. 9027. 9190.
#> 5 matrix_2pl_f1_configural.rds   -4474. 9043. 9262.

Other mirt functions. A ModelRecord doesn’t store the full mirt model object. model_from_record() rebuilds it from the stored parameters and data (without re-estimating anything), so you can use other mirt functions, e.g. for item fit or plots:

mod <- model_from_record(mod_rec)
mirt::itemfit(mirt::extract.group(mod, group = "site_a"))
#>           item   S_X2 df.S_X2 RMSEA.S_X2 p.S_X2
#> 1  matrix_01-1  3.737      10      0.000  0.958
#> 2  matrix_02-1 11.247      10      0.018  0.339
#> 3  matrix_03-1 10.100      11      0.000  0.521
#> 4  matrix_04-1  5.605      10      0.000  0.847
#> 5  matrix_05-1  4.807      10      0.000  0.904
#> 6  matrix_06-1  6.420      10      0.000  0.779
#> 7  matrix_07-1  7.653      10      0.000  0.663
#> 8  matrix_08-1 14.382      10      0.033  0.156
#> 9  matrix_09-1 11.731      10      0.021  0.303
#> 10 matrix_10-1 19.123      11      0.043  0.059
#> 11 matrix_11-1  4.248      11      0.000  0.962
#> 12 matrix_12-1 12.705      11      0.020  0.313
#> 13 matrix_13-1  7.372       9      0.000  0.598
#> 14 matrix_14-1  6.047       9      0.000  0.735
#> 15 matrix_15-1  9.282       9      0.009  0.412

Other contents are available as slots, e.g. mod_rec@data (the response matrix, with columns in items(mod_rec) order), mod_rec@groups (group of each row), and model_vals(mod_rec) (the full mirt::mod2values() parameter table).

Using real LEVANTE data

To fit models to real data, build task_data from the raw (unprocessed) per-site LEVANTE datasets. process_trials() loads their trials, drops practice trials, incomplete runs, and invalid runs, and adds item identifiers and metadata. Language comes from the run data and dataset from the participant data, and recode_trials() then makes the trials ready for scoring:

dataset_spec <- list(
  list(name = "pilot_western_ca_main_raw:97mt", version = "v15_28")
)

runs <- process_runs(dataset_spec)
participants <- process_participants(dataset_spec)

task_data <- process_trials(dataset_spec) |>
  left_join(runs |> select(run_id, language), by = "run_id") |>
  left_join(participants |> select(user_id, dataset), by = "user_id") |>
  recode_trials() |>
  nest(data = -c(item_task, dataset, language))

The production LEVANTE models also apply further exclusions before fitting (e.g. duplicate runs, straightlining, responses that are too fast or too slow, and items flagged for exclusion). These exclusions are applied in the levante-pilots repository, in 01_fetch_data/02_scoring_prep.qmd, and the models are fit in 02_score_data/01_fit_irt/01_fit_irt_modular.qmd, which runs the fits above for every task in parallel.
